NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) Q2 2025 Earnings Call Transcript August 28, 2024.

Executives Present:
Jensen Huang - President and Chief Executive Officer
Colette Kress - Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer
Stewart Stecker - Vice President of Investor Relations

Analysts Present:
Toshiya Hari - Goldman Sachs
C.J. Muse - Cantor Fitzgerald
Vivek Arya - Bank of America Securities
Stacy Rasgon - Bernstein Research
Joe Moore - Morgan Stanley

[SECTION: PREPARED_REMARKS]
Operator: Good afternoon. My name is Kevin, and I will be your conference operator today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to NVIDIA's Second Quarter Fiscal 2025 Earnings Conference Call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session.

Stewart Stecker: Thank you, Kevin. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NVIDIA's conference call for the second quarter of fiscal 2025. With me today are Jensen Huang, NVIDIA's President and Chief Executive Officer; and Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Today's call is being webcast on the NVIDIA Investor Relations website.

Colette Kress: Thanks, Stewart. Q2 was another record quarter. Revenue of $30.04 billion was up 15% sequentially and up 122% year-on-year, well above our outlook of $28.0 billion. Data Center revenue of $26.3 billion was up 16% sequentially and up 154% year-on-year, driven by strong demand for our Hopper architecture GPU computing platform for training and inferencing large language models, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications.

Cloud service providers represented roughly 45% of our Data Center revenue, and more than 50% came from enterprise and consumer internet companies. Networking revenue was $3.7 billion, up 16% sequentially and up 114% year-on-year, driven by our Quantum-2 InfiniBand platform and our Spectrum-X Ethernet networking platform for AI.

Moving to Gaming. Gaming revenue was $2.88 billion, up 9% sequentially and up 16% year-on-year, reflecting higher shipments of GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs. Professional Visualization revenue was $454 million, up 6% sequentially and up 20% year-on-year. Automotive revenue was $346 million, up 5% sequentially and up 37% year-on-year, driven by self-driving platforms.

Gross margin for the quarter was 75.1% GAAP and 75.7% non-GAAP. GAAP operating expenses were $3.93 billion, and non-GAAP operating expenses were $2.79 billion. We returned $7.4 billion to shareholders in the form of share repurchases and cash dividends. Our Board of Directors approved an additional $50 billion in share repurchase authorization.

Let me now address Blackwell. We shipped customer samples of our Blackwell architecture in the second quarter. We incorporated a change to the Blackwell GPU mask to improve production yield. Blackwell production ramp is scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter and continue into fiscal 2026. In the fourth quarter, we expect to ship several billion dollars of Blackwell revenue. Demand for Blackwell platforms is well ahead of supply, and we expect this to continue into next year. Hopper demand is strong, and shipments are expected to increase in the second half of fiscal 2025.

Outlook for the third quarter of fiscal 2025: Revenue is expected to be $32.5 billion, plus or minus 2%. GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 74.4% and 75.0%, respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points. For the full year, we expect gross margins to be in the mid-70% range. GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $4.3 billion and $3.0 billion, respectively.

Jensen Huang: Thanks, Colette. NVIDIA achieved record revenues as global data centers are in full throttle to modernize the entire computing stack with accelerated computing and generative AI. Blackwell samples are shipping to our partners and customers. Generative AI will revolutionize every industry.

[SECTION: ANALYST_QA]
Operator: Your first question comes from the line of Toshiya Hari with Goldman Sachs.
Toshiya Hari: Hi, thank you so much for taking the question. Jensen, I wanted to ask about Blackwell and Hopper dynamics. You mentioned the mask change to improve production yields on Blackwell. Could you provide more color on the nature of that change? And secondly, how should we think about Hopper demand sustaining while customers wait for Blackwell to ramp?

Jensen Huang: Thanks, Toshiya. First, let's talk about the Blackwell mask change. The functionality of Blackwell was complete from the start. Blackwell has 7 different chips that make up the architecture: the Blackwell GPU, the Grace CPU, the ConnectX-7 NIC, the BlueField-3 DPU, NVLink switches, and our optical transceivers. We made a mask modification to the Blackwell silicon to improve yield. There were no functional changes necessary. As a result, we will begin production ramp in Q4. We shipped engineering samples worldwide in Q2 and will ship production units starting in Q4.

Now on Hopper demand: Hopper demand is accelerating, not slowing down. Why? Because the race to train frontier models and deploy real-time inference is urgent. Companies that invest in compute now generate returns immediately. Customers cannot afford to pause for six months; every month of delayed compute means losing market leadership. Hopper supply is increasing, and we will ship more Hoppers in Q3 and Q4 than in Q1 and Q2.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Vivek Arya with Bank of America Securities.
Vivek Arya: Thanks for taking my question. Colette, regarding the gross margin trajectory: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 75.7%, and Q3 guidance is 75.0%. As Blackwell begins its ramp in Q4, should we anticipate gross margin dilution during the initial ramp phase before stabilizing in the mid-70s?

Colette Kress: Vivek, thank you for the question. Yes, let me walk you through our gross margin profile. As we start ramping Blackwell in the fourth quarter, initial manufacturing yields and the introduction of complex new packaging technologies like CoWoS-L and liquid-cooled NVLink racks will initially carry slightly lower gross margins. We anticipate gross margins in Q4 to experience a moderate headwind, likely landing in the low-70% range during the first couple of quarters of ramp. However, as yields optimize and volume ramps throughout fiscal 2026, we expect gross margins to rebound swiftly back to the mid-70% range. Our full-year gross margin expectation for fiscal 2025 remains firmly in the mid-70% range.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Stacy Rasgon with Bernstein Research.
Stacy Rasgon: Thanks guys. Colette, regarding the $50 billion share repurchase authorization: can you discuss your capital allocation philosophy? You generated massive free cash flow this quarter. Why buy back shares at current multiples rather than expanding M&A or fab investments?

Colette Kress: Thanks, Stacy. Our capital allocation strategy is disciplined and focused. First and foremost, we fully fund our R&D and organic growth initiatives. We are investing aggressively in our roadmap across silicon, software, and systems architecture. Second, we evaluate strategic ecosystem investments and selective M&A where appropriate. However, given our cash generation and strong balance sheet, returning capital to shareholders via repurchases reflects our supreme confidence in our multi-year growth trajectory and sovereign AI expansion.
